comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Stock Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD returned $862 million to shareholders in 2024 through stock repurchases, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific share repurchase volumes and remaining authorization under a repurchase program aimed at offsetting dilution or returning capital. NVDA reports repurchasing 2.8 million shares for $1.9 billion in early fiscal 2025 under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, explicitly stating the goal is to offset dilution from employee share issuances. Similarly, AMD reports returning $862 million through the repurchase of 5.9 million shares during fiscal 2024, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date.

sentences.text: From January 29, 2024 through February 16, 2024, we repurchased 2.8 million shares for $1.9 billion pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan.
Our share repurchase program aims to offset dilution from shares issued to employees.
During the twelve months ended December 28, 2024, we returned a total of $862 million to shareholders through the repurchase of 5.9 million shares of common stock under our stock repurchase program.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
